note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Knee pain and clicking, worse with running and certain gym movements.
- Onset/duration: ~2 weeks.
- Progression: Worsening with recent longer runs; most recent run required stopping due to pain.
- Laterality/location: Predominantly right knee pain; initially mentioned “knees” clicking, later clarified left knee asymptomatic (conflict noted). Pain felt centrally and slightly to the right of the right knee.
- Triggers/timing: Pain begins ~20 minutes into runs (~mile 2.5–3). Clicking noted during ab exercises requiring knee flexion/extension. No pain at rest currently.
- Associated symptoms: One episode of tingling in right toes after a run (resolved). Intermittent sock indentation after prolonged standing; no persistent leg swelling reported.
- Prior injuries: Ice hockey fall months ago with large bruise; no ongoing issues.
- Functional impact: Can walk normally; no issues on stairs. Can continue short distance after pain starts but recently stopped due to worsening symptoms.
- Relevant negatives: No giving way/instability, no locking, no persistent swelling currently, no calf pain, no color/temperature change in legs, no foot/arch pain, no ongoing numbness/tingling.
- Context: Training for a marathon (runs 4–8 miles; started about a month ago). Gym a few times per week.

Past Medical History:
- Conditions: Farsightedness.
- Surgeries/procedures: LASIK eye surgery.
- Significant past illness/hospital/ER: Severe UTI previously; evaluated in ER with concern for kidney stones.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen, patient-reported up to 400 mg as needed.
  - Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Aleve (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Xanax (alprazolam) occasionally for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Recreational cannabis: “smoke a joint” occasionally.
- GI/asthma/reflux: Denied.

Physical Examination:
- Telemedicine visit; no vitals recorded.
- Right knee:
  - No current visible swelling per patient.
  - Full range of motion: able to fully flex and extend.
  - No locking, no instability/giving way.
  - Pain occurs with running after ~20 minutes; clicking during certain gym activities (ab exercises involving knee motion).
- Gait/Function: No difficulty walking or with stairs.
- Neurovascular: One prior transient episode of right toe tingling post-run; resolved. No persistent sensory changes; no color/temperature change reported.
- Calf: No pain reported.

Impression:
- Right knee pain with activity and intermittent mechanical symptoms in the context of recent increase in running volume—likely overuse injury; structural pathology (e.g., cartilage/meniscal/ligamentous) not ruled out.

Management Plan:
- Continue ice therapy regularly to the knee.
- Reduce running load; avoid running through pain. Pause activity if pain necessitates stopping.
- Prescribed a stronger anti-inflammatory to take regularly with food; not to be taken concurrently with ibuprofen. Specific medication and dosing not documented; prescription sent to pharmacy.
- Referral to physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment and targeted rehabilitation.
- Consider imaging after physiotherapy evaluation if indicated to assess for intra-articular pathology.
- Safety net: Seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks (unable to bend/straighten).

Patient Summary:
- Patient training for a marathon developed right knee pain starting ~2 weeks ago, provoked by running and certain exercises, with one brief episode of post-run toe tingling. No instability, locking, or current swelling.
- Clinician suspects overuse-related knee injury; plan includes activity modification, ice, a stronger anti-inflammatory, and physiotherapy, with imaging considered based on assessment or if symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Do not run through pain; reduce or pause runs until assessed and symptoms improve.
- Use ice therapy frequently; take the prescribed anti-inflammatory with food and do not combine it with ibuprofen.
- Seek urgent care for swelling with heat/redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks.

Next Steps:
- Attend physiotherapy appointment for detailed evaluation and rehab plan.
- Pick up and start the prescribed anti-inflammatory as directed; avoid concurrent NSAIDs.
- Follow up with the clinic if wait for physio is prolonged, symptoms worsen, or not improving; imaging may be arranged if indicated.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not documented; no vitals; no detailed musculoskeletal exam maneuvers; medication reconciliation (names/doses/routes/frequencies) incomplete; past orthopedic history limited.
- Internal conflicts: Patient initially reported “knees” hurting/clicking but later stated pain is only in the right knee; left knee asymptomatic (conflict noted). Clicking not present at rest during call but reported at gym/with certain movements.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional filler and brief interruptions, but clinically usable.
